sources.summary: Jacques Forestier/Boris Kusnezow (Warner Classics) The Canadian violinist’s album definitely does what it says on the tin: from Bartók to Ernst, there is a quiet and beguiling eloquence to his playing Perhaps the most promising thing about this impressive debut album from Jacques Forestier , the young Canadian violinist who tied in first place at the 2024 Joseph Joachim Competition, is the way it lives up to its title. There’s a swing to the way he and the pianist Boris Kusnezow play Bartók’s six Romanian Folk Dances that extends even into the quiet movements, which sound distant and beguiling. Wieniawski’s Polonaise de Concert comes across as a dance rather than just a flashy showpiece. Bach’s D minor Sarabande is framed by movements from Ysaÿe’s solo Sonatas. All have persuasive rhythmic poise. Continue reading...
